machine: Apple M5 Pro, 20 GPU cores, 24GB, macOS 26.5.1
power: AC power, 100% battery reported. No GPU frequency lock.
same_inputs: All 12 input token-ID SHA256 values match across both Python/tokenizer environments; same checkpoint paths and exact raw prompts.
configuration: Greedy, batch 1, unquantized full KV, fresh request state, 128 output tokens. Monolith: autotune+commute_norm, attention auto, capacity 8704, prefill64. MLX uses unmodified generators: native plain prefill2048/N7 prefill512, then prefill64 for both. Same NVFP4 Qwen3 8B and affine-INT4 Qwen3 0.6B.
order: One resident engine/process, serial requests. At 4K: MLX then Monolith per mode; at 8K the order reverses. Then MLX prefill64 sensitivity runs. Finally 3-prompt plain controls with both MLX prefill sizes and reversed engine order at 8K. Exact launches retained.

timing.monolith: Generation.decode_wall_ms/127 for per-output latency; /len(accepted) for N7 round average.
timing.mlx: First-to-last native token yield /127 for per-output latency. Full N7 round intervals between consecutive non-draft yields whose proposed count is seven. First round and shortened tail rounds excluded; no detokenization in timed loop.
timing.caveats: MLX first yield follows an entire verification round, so its first-to-last per-token timer excludes computation for other tokens in that first burst. Monolith terminal round may skip its following draft chain. These endpoints slightly favor opposite engines on the two metrics.
timing.round_bound: Monolith total decode wall/(executed rounds-1) bounds the average of the preceding completed full cycles from above: charge all terminal/queued work to those cycles. Every measured prompt still beats each corresponding MLX full-round mean.
timing.drift: Absolute latency shifted between blocks with unchanged Monolith cache/pack and 24/24 identical output+acceptance sequences versus the prior tuning run. Late MLX plain controls converge for both prefill sizes, so do not attribute the initial large shift to prefill size alone.

limits: One prompt family and two context lengths. Generated outputs differ across engines and prefill modes; not a reference-accuracy or universal workload claim. No meaningful plain-decode advantage is established.
